reason: The action part (no build, slot or pair change; keep decision B; do not re-ask) is harmless and feasible, but the VALUE claim does not hold. (1) The evidence is in-sample for the detector: the x138-family detectors were trained on all 199 train videos (CONTEXT l.1071, Eric 742064: local +0.0078 became -0.002 on LB), so annotated cells on the 4 dummy clips carry high trained scores. Any ILP cost change that prunes low-score nodes will be depleted near GT by construction. The 4-vs-28.3 (7x) depletion is this selection effect and says nothing about unseen embryos. (2) Even in-sample the removed set sits at break-even. CONTEXT l.2347 (metric re-audit) says the node-drop bonus pays only when P(annotated) < ~0.2%, and the near-GT rate of the removed nodes is 4/1812 = 0.22%. TP/FP/FN stay unchanged only because none of those 4 is a matched annotated node. (3) The payoff is asymmetric. The node bonus is capped at about +0.0007 (-939 nodes x ~3.1e-6). One lost annotated node costs about 2/530 GT edges, ~-0.0035 per clip. With ~453 removed nodes per clip, an out-of-sample annotated rate of only 0.1% (still ~15x depleted against the 1.56% base) already costs ~-0.0016 and outweighs the bonus. The private range is therefore about -0.003..+0.0007, not 0..+0.0007. (4) A DIS removal has already cost a TP in-sample (exp88a on exp70g: -0.0008, 1 TP), and the exp13 48-video parabola gives -0.0007 at 2.25. (5) The only out-of-sample read, public dd = 0 from probes 52/54, fits bonus ~ loss better than a clean structural +0.0007. So 'public-only is too strong' and 'the read now has a mechanism' are not established. The node multiplier is linear, but whether the removed nodes are unannotated on the new embryo is exactly the untested premise.
